sections.heading: Indus Valley Civilization — origin, extent & chronology

blocks.text: The **Indus Valley (Harappan) Civilization** was the **first urbanisation of the Indian subcontinent** and one of the world's three earliest riverine civilisations (with Mesopotamia and Egypt). It belonged to the **Bronze Age**, spread over ~**1.3 million sq km** — the **largest** of the contemporary Bronze-Age civilisations — and is dated (mature phase) to **c. 2600–1900 BCE**.

rows: **Harappa** first excavated by **Daya Ram Sahni (1921)**; **Mohenjo-daro** by **R.D. Banerji (1922)**; both under **Sir John Marshall** (announced the civilisation, 1924).
After the **Indus (Sindhu)** river; also 'Harappan' after the first-found site (naming after first-discovered site is convention).
Now often called **Indus–Saraswati** civilisation — most sites lie along the dried **Ghaggar-Hakra (Saraswati)** bed.
Skeletal remains: **Mediterranean, Proto-Australoid, Mongoloid, Alpine** — a mixed population.
Regional farming cultures (Hakra, Ravi, Kot Diji); proto-urban; e.g. **Mehrgarh** (7000 BCE, Neolithic ancestor).
Full urbanism — planned cities, seals, standard weights, long-distance trade.
De-urbanisation; regionalisation (Cemetery H, Jhukar, Rangpur); transition to Chalcolithic villages.

**Mohenjo-daro** ('Mound of the Dead') — R.D. Banerji (1922), River **Indus**, Larkana; Sindhi.

Corner sites: **Manda (N), Daimabad (S), Sutkagendor (W), Alamgirpur (E)**.
**Rakhigarhi (Haryana)** = largest site; **Dholavira & Lothal** = the two Indian **UNESCO** IVC sites (Dholavira inscribed 2021).
Script **undeciphered**, written **boustrophedon**; number system likely **decimal**; weights in **binary (1,2,4,8…)** then decimal multiples.
**Mehrgarh** (Balochistan, 7000 BCE) — Neolithic precursor: earliest farming & animal domestication in the subcontinent.
Sir **John Marshall** announced the discovery (1924) in the *Illustrated London News*.
Most sites on the dried **Ghaggar-Hakra (Saraswati)** system → 'Indus–Saraswati' civilisation.

blocks.text: The **Indus/Harappan Civilisation** spread across a vast area of the north-west subcontinent, with major cities strung along the **Indus and (dried) Saraswati-Ghaggar-Hakra** systems. Each key site — **Harappa, Mohenjodaro, Dholavira, Lothal, Kalibangan, Rakhigarhi** — is associated with distinctive finds that are frequent exam facts.

rows: **Ravi** (Punjab, Pakistan); first excavated (1921, Daya Ram Sahni); granaries, cemetery R-37, workmen's quarters.
**Indus** (Sindh, Pakistan); **Great Bath, Great Granary, Dancing Girl, Priest-King, Pashupati seal**.
**Rann of Kutch (Gujarat)**; unique **water-harvesting/reservoirs**, signboard, three-part city; **UNESCO site**.
**Gujarat (Bhogava)**; **dockyard** (maritime trade), bead factory, rice husk, fire-altars.
**Haryana** — the **largest IVC site** in India (Ghaggar plain).

sections.heading: 📊 Integrated: IVC sites at a glance

rows: Great Bath, granary, advanced drainage, planned streets.
Water conservation system, three-tiered city structure.
Fire altars, grid pattern streets, ploughed fields.

items: **River-site pairs**: Harappa–Ravi, Mohenjo-daro–Indus, Kalibangan–Ghaggar, Lothal–Bhogava, Dholavira–Rann of Kutch.
**Signature finds**: Great Bath & Dancing Girl (Mohenjo-daro), dockyard & rice (Lothal), ploughed field & fire altars (Kalibangan), water reservoirs & signboard (Dholavira), horse bones? (Surkotada).

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: the sites & their signature finds

rows: Granaries (6+6 rows), coffin/Cemetery **R-37 & H**, red-sandstone torso, stone dancing figure, mother-goddess figurines, phallus/lingam-yoni.
**Great Bath**, Great Granary (largest building), **bronze Dancing Girl**, **Pashupati seal**, steatite **'Priest-King'**, bearded man, assembly hall, woven cotton.
**3-part city** (citadel+middle+lower), giant **water reservoirs & dams**, stadium, the **10-letter signboard**; UNESCO 2021.
**Dockyard** (tidal harbour), bead factory, rice husk, fire-altars, painted jar (crow-and-deer 'thirsty crow'), Persian-Gulf seal, terracotta ship.
World's earliest **ploughed field**, **fire-altars** (ritual), wooden drainage, bones of camel, 'city of bangles'.
Only city with **no citadel**; bead-making, lipstick, ink-well, cat chasing dog footprints; famous bronze bullock-cart.
Both **pre-Harappan & Harappan** levels; radial streets; terracotta plough, barley.
Largest site; aDNA study on skeletons; granary, drains.

blocks.text: Memory hook: **water** cities are in **Gujarat** (Dholavira reservoirs, Lothal dockyard); the **ploughed field & fire-altars** = Kalibangan; **no-citadel** = Chanhudaro; **horse bones** = Surkotada.

items: Match site to signature find: Mohenjodaro-Great Bath/Dancing Girl, Lothal-dockyard, Kalibangan-ploughed field, Dholavira-water reservoirs, Rakhigarhi-largest in India.
Harappa was the first site excavated (1921); rivers: Harappa-Ravi, Mohenjodaro-Indus.

prelimsPointers: **Harappa (Ravi, Pakistan)** — first excavated in **1921** (Daya Ram Sahni); granaries, cemetery R-37.
**Mohenjodaro (Indus, Sindh)** — **Great Bath, Great Granary, Dancing Girl, Priest-King, Pashupati seal**.
**Dholavira (Kutch, Gujarat)** — advanced **water-harvesting & reservoirs**; 'signboard'; a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
**Lothal (Gujarat)** — **dockyard** (evidence of maritime trade); bead-making; fire-altars.
**Kalibangan (Rajasthan, Ghaggar)** — **ploughed field**, fire-altars, earthquake evidence.
**Rakhigarhi (Haryana)** — the **largest Harappan site in India**.
Other sites — **Chanhudaro (beads, no citadel), Banawali, Surkotada (horse bones debated), Ropar**.
**Rakhigarhi (Haryana)** — largest IVC site in India; **Dholavira & Lothal** are the Indian UNESCO IVC sites.
**Chanhudaro** — only IVC city without a citadel; bead-making. **Banawali** — both pre-Harappan & Harappan levels.
**Great Bath & Dancing Girl & Pashupati seal → Mohenjo-daro**; **granaries & torso → Harappa**.
**Dockyard → Lothal**; **ploughed field & fire-altars → Kalibangan**; **water reservoirs & signboard → Dholavira**.
**Chanhudaro** — only city without a citadel; **Surkotada** — horse bones; **Rakhigarhi** — largest & aDNA site.
**Daimabad** (Maharashtra) — famous bronze chariot; southernmost site.
